contract: C12, the control door: docs/contracts/C12.md (board ab-v16.94.1). One JSON object per line on the service's control.sock. The daemon sends the requests (req); the service sends the answers (res) and the events (ev). Each request carries its provenance (by). The service and the daemon test against the same lines. The service's state for these lines, and the fake's state at its start (agent-browser service --fake): state. Its open prompts are p1 (host login.example, list owner-repo) and p2 (host cdn.example, list owner-repo); its list owner-repo holds a.example and old.example. The reads q1 to q5 give the keys of the data of status, lists_get, prompts_get, endpoint and sender (stage 1a, board ab-v16.94.2). Since board ab-v16.94.5 (stage 1d; the token design, board ab-v16.94.10) each item of set_sessions carries mcp_token, the fingerprint of the session's connection token or null; the bad lines b22 to b32 break each rule of mcp_token; r14 is the daemon's snapshot while two live sessions have one launch name (live: the daemon's live sessions); testTokens are made-up test values in a token's form, with their fingerprints. The stored sign-ins (board ab-v16.97.1, the part "The stored sign-ins" of C12): the requests s1 to s57 run in their order after r14 (s53 after s17, s54 after s10, s55 after s13, s56 after s36, s57 after s38, s58 and s59 after s51) with the fake values of state.sign_ins (the fake opens no seal), the bad requests b33 to b53 refuse a kind, a shape or a rule of record, unprotected holds the cases of a protection that does not hold (each on a new fake with --unprotected and its reason; failing names each protection that does not hold), and signInScan holds the canaries of the scan. Board ab-v16.97.2: each pane's seal is a real seal of agentwatch's screen-seal.js to the test pane key of paneSeal (test/vectors/sign-in-seals.mjs writes them), and paneSeal holds one shared seal with its binding, its bytes, its test keys and its payload; the real service answers these lines too, with its own key and sealed parts in the later sign_ins (C12, the vectors). busy holds the case of a full queue (lines in one write: C12, the vectors).

paneSeal.note: TEST keys and values only, never a real key or secret. The test pane key: its private half is SHA-256 of "test, not a key: the pane key of the stored sign-ins' vectors", its public half is state.sign_ins.pane_key. Each pane's seal of the requests is a seal of agentwatch's screen-seal.js (sealPayload) to it, with the binding of its request and the test keys SHA-256 of "test, not a key: ephemeral <request id>" and "test, not a key: sender <request id>"; test/vectors/sign-in-seals.mjs writes them. vector is one seal with its binding, the binding's bytes, its test keys and its payload.

busy.note: The bound of the queue of sign_ins_setup, sign_ins_unlock and sign_ins_rekey (C12, the passphrase; the daemon lead's condition of review-118b). On a new fake or service: the lines of first run in their order, each after its answer; then the lines of pipelined go in one write. busy-5 holds the vectors' wrong_passphrase (s28's seal), so it runs for 2 s; busy-6 and busy-7 wait behind it; busy-8 is one more, and it gets the busy text at once. order gives the ids in the order of their answers. The real service answers busy-2 with its own key, and a test sends that key in busy-3 in place of the vectors' key.

res.error: the store is busy; try again

refusalRate.note: The rate of the refusal ends of the sign-in act (C11, C12; PR #112's open point 11, the daemon lead's rule): an end with no start. At most limit of them for one scope in any window_ms; a further one is not sent, and the service counts it. The next refusal end of the scope that goes after such ones carries dropped, their number, and it goes only when at least window_ms have passed since the scope's last refusal end that went. Each scope on its own. at_ms is the service's clock; send says whether the end goes.

checkTwo.note: C11's check 2 and C12's names and ids (PR #112's open point 4): the record that the sign-in act uses for a name is the one record of the last sign_ins with that name whose plain fields have their shape and whose approved is true. Two approved records of one name each break, so check 2 finds neither, and the act answers no_such_name. An offer that waits (approved false) is no such record, also when an approved record has its name. A record that breaks its shape is none. The sealed parts are no real seals: check 2 reads the plain fields only (whether a record opens is check 5's). usable is what AgentBrowser.signIns can list (before the scope's list).

cardPay.note: The card payments (C12, the part "The card payments"; board goal ab-sta; C11, the card payment). requests: each op with its answer for a service whose hello has the feature card_pay (no service and no fake has it yet); withoutFeature: the answer of a service without it (the service and the fake today). Each seal and sealed part is a stand-in of the right form: no real seal, and no value of a card. events: the payment's events (each pay_request carries earlier, and each request that had a pay_request gets one pay_result). orderHash: the order of the first pay_request and its page-order hash (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its compact JSON with sorted keys and no ASCII escapes), and the hash of the same order with another line.

opBinding.note: The binding of a pane's seal names its op (C12, the pane's seal of the card form; the daemon lead's point at the OK of PR #224): a seal that the pane made for one op does not open as the other op. Each seal here is a REAL seal of agentwatch's screen-seal.js (sealPayload) to the vectors' test pane key (paneSeal), with the binding madeFor and the test keys SHA-256 of "test, not a key: ephemeral <request id>" and "test, not a key: sender <request id>" (test/vectors/sign-in-seals.mjs writes them). The seal of o1 holds the canaries of signInScan; the seal of o2 holds payload, stand-in values of the card form, no value of a card. A store at each seal's time answers res: the binding of the request's own op is not the seal's.
